correctness.rationale: Gaussian STFT Hermite diagonalization gives the stated exact incomplete-gamma eigenvalues and orthogonal modes. Integration by parts makes their sequence unimodal, reducing the restricted minimum to indices 0 and K. The endpoint ratio is strictly increasing in inner radius and crosses once. The K-th eigenvalue is rising at the crossing and has a unique single peak, while the zero-th decreases everywhere; this gives the unique global maximum and precise two-mode equality. Stirling expansion of the crossing integral gives \(K/e\), its exact logarithmic and constant terms, and the prefactor of the exponentially small optimum. The packaged standard-library program independently checks finite spectra and asymptotic convergence, not infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: Maximizing the smallest restricted concentration eigenvalue is the exact finite-band stability/observability design problem for a specified Hermite signal class. The full all-K exact optimization and two-dimensional unique worst-mode family determine a natural complete invariant; the sharp \(K/e\) relocation and logarithmic prefactor quantify its bandwidth cost. This is not a mere new name for a known top-eigenvalue formula or a finite table. Limits are single concentric annuli, Gaussian windows and fixed positive area.
